title: Self-Reporting, Notification and Early Engagement
summary: When and how the firm should tell the authority about a potential breach, how candour affects the outcome, and how to shape scope and timetable through early engagement.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: When and how the firm should tell the authority about a potential breach, how candour affects the outcome, and how to shape scope and timetable through early engagement.
Learning Objectives: Apply notification duties and judge when a self-report is required or advisable
Explain how openness and timely self-reporting influence enforcement outcomes
Plan early engagement with the authority on scope, timing and the firm's own review
Syllabus: Notification duties, materiality and the expectation of openness
Self-reporting: timing, content and what the authority will do with it
Running an internal review alongside or ahead of the authority's investigation
Scoping meetings, case teams and agreeing a realistic timetable
Intended Audience: Chief executives, senior managers and directors who may be accountable when the firm is investigated
Heads of compliance, risk, internal audit and financial crime, and their deputies
General counsel, in-house lawyers and company secretaries who coordinate the firm's response
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of compliance, legal or senior management work in a regulated firm is helpful. No prior experience of enforcement proceedings is required.
Core Reading: IOSCO, Credible Deterrence in the Enforcement of Securities Regulation (2015)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
IOSCO, Multilateral Memorandum of Understanding (MMoU) and Enhanced MMoU (2016)
